# Mike Basios — full profile

Automatic software optimisation by search · Co-founder & CTO, [TurinTech AI](https://turintech.ai) · London. Canonical page: https://mike-turintech.github.io/ (short version: https://mike-turintech.github.io/llms.txt)

## About

I work on automatic software optimisation: search methods that change code, models and AI agents, and keep the changes that measure better. I have worked on this since my PhD at University College London, and since 2017 as co-founder and CTO of [TurinTech AI](https://turintech.ai), a UCL spinout in London.

The core idea has stayed the same over the years. Treat a program as something with many possible versions. Generate candidates: at first by swapping data structures and tuning parameters, now also with language models proposing edits. Run each candidate on the real workload. Measure it on several objectives at once, such as runtime, memory, accuracy and cost. Keep the ones that are better, and search again from there. TurinTech's product, [Artemis](https://www.turintech.ai/product/overview), is this loop built for production code. Its Discovery mode runs the loop on its own from a stated goal. Changes it found have been merged by the maintainers of NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp and OpenAI Whisper; the pull requests and benchmarks are [public](https://www.turintech.ai/open-source).

My part in that: the original research and the first version of Artemis, in my thesis, where it selected data structures for 44 Java programs; the design of the current system; and the first version of Discovery. On the papers since then I set the research questions and the experiments together with the team, and they do most of the building and the writing.

What I want to work on next is search that improves its own search: systems that form hypotheses about a codebase or a model, run the experiments, and use what they learn to choose the next ones. Some people call this autoresearch. Our work on evolving LLM-based agents is a first step.

I studied informatics at the University of Piraeus (BSc, first class) and computer science at the University of Edinburgh (MSc with distinction), started research at Edinburgh with Stratis Viglas, and moved to UCL for the PhD, supervised by Earl Barr with Ilya Sergey. [The thesis](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10070648/) was published at ESEC/FSE, ICSE, ASE and SSBSE and received an ACM GECCO [Human-Competitive Results (Humies)](https://www.human-competitive.org/) award in 2019. Before TurinTech I worked on data and software systems at BNP Paribas and Commerzbank.

I have taught and supervised throughout. I ran the lab for Edinburgh's Extreme Computing course (Hadoop, Spark). At UCL I supervised MSc theses and projects, many placed with banks and technology companies. At TurinTech I have co-supervised PhD students; several have defended and others are in progress. Most of my papers are joint work with researchers at UCL, Leeds (an Innovate UK Knowledge Transfer Partnership), Surrey, King's College London and Warwick, with support from a Horizon 2020 grant. The company started with evoML, which applied the same search to machine-learning models, before we generalised it to code. Away from work I play 9-a-side football.

## Publications

Full record on [DBLP](https://dblp.org/pid/123/5293), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=8r8p0skAAAAJ) (1,100+ citations, h-index 10) and [Semantic Scholar](https://www.semanticscholar.org/author/Michail-Basios/2907390). Listed as Michail Basios in most venues. Selected: search-based and LLM-guided software optimisation, evolutionary computation and the research behind Artemis; a few finance side-projects are omitted.
